source: MAFF/partner document, "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop), Section III: Physical/botanical characteristics of corn
text:
Corn is a plant with a short life cycle suited to cultivation, maturing in about 85, 90, 110, 130, or up to 185 days depending on variety. Most corn varieties grown in Cambodia mature in 85, 90, or 110 days.

Corn plants typically reach a height of about 1.5-3 meters; in South America, some corn varieties can grow up to 9 meters tall.

The leaves are long and blade-shaped, about 1 meter long and 7-15 cm wide, emerging from the stem nodes and alternating from one side to the other up the stalk. A distinctive feature of the corn plant is that a single plant carries both a male flower and a female flower, but on different parts of the plant: the male flower (tassel) is at the top of the plant, while the female flower (ear/silk) is located partway up, at the middle of the stalk -- and it is this female flower that becomes the site where the corn ear (grain) develops.
